newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures were both expected to open 0.250 to 1.000 cent higher following Friday's bullishly construed monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report, analysts said.
Friday's cattle report showed December placements well under trade expectations and this should spark early demand, especially in April and June live cattle futures, analysts said.
The report put placements at 98 percent of a year ago, well under the average estimate of 108.2 percent and the range of estimates of 103 to 112 percent.
However, February live cattle may show scale up resistance from the continued weak tone to cash beef and expectations of larger near term supplies of fed cattle, analysts said.

The Cattle-on-Feed Report was also viewed as bullish for feeder cattle. Feeder prices have been rising lately even with the low feedlot placements last month, and this points to tight feeder supplies. Calls for lower corn futures should also lend support, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.03 at $70.18 per cwt.
